primary_source: A.-E. Beguyer de Chancourtois, "Memoire sur un classement naturel des corps simples ou radicaux, appele vis tellurique", Comptes rendus hebdomadaires des seances de l'Academie des sciences (Paris: Mallet-Bachelier), vol. 54 (1862), pp. 757-761, with continuations pp. 840-843 and 967-971
organising_principle: Elements plotted by atomic weight along a helix wound on a vertical cylinder whose circumference is divided into 16 units (approx. the atomic weight of oxygen); one full turn = 16 weight units; chemically similar elements fall on the same vertical generator line
successful_predictions: First published recognition that elemental properties recur periodically as a function of atomic weight (e.g. O above S on the same generator); no confirmed predictions of specific new elements; impact was limited because the printer omitted the folding diagram from the Comptes rendus printing

primary_source: D. I. Mendeleev, "Sootnoshenie svoistv s atomnym vesom elementov", Zhurnal Russkogo Khimicheskogo Obshchestva 1 (1869), pp. 60-77; German abstract Zeitschrift fuer Chemie 12 (1869), pp. 405-406; full elaboration "Die periodische Gesetzmaessigkeit der chemischen Elemente", Annalen der Chemie und Pharmacie, Supplementband 8 (1871), pp. 133-229
organising_principle: Elements ordered by atomic weight; properties are a periodic function of atomic weight; deliberate gaps left where the sequence demanded unknown elements, with quantitative property predictions for the missing members
successful_predictions: Eka-aluminium confirmed as gallium (Lecoq de Boisbaudran, 1875); eka-boron confirmed as scandium (Nilson, 1879); eka-silicon confirmed as germanium (Winkler, 1886) - predicted atomic weights, densities and oxide chemistry matched measurement; also corrected accepted atomic weights (e.g. Be, U)
citation: https://web.lemoyne.edu/giunta/ea/mendeleevann.html (English translation of the 1871 Annalen paper with full bibliographic data, retrieved 2026-09-11); https://www.historyofinformation.com/detail.php?id=2898 (1869 bibliographic record, retrieved 2026-09-11)

primary_source: Charles Janet, "Essais de classification helicoidale des elements chimiques", Beauvais: Imprimerie departementale de l'Oise, November 1928 (79 pp. + folding tables); English summary "The helicoidal classification of the elements", Chemical News 138 (1929), pp. 372-374 and 388-393
organising_principle: Strict ordering by atomic number with rows defined by the n+l sum of the filling subshell (left-step form): row lengths 2,2,8,8,18,18,32,32; s-block moved to the right edge; helium placed above beryllium; derived from an underlying helical construction
successful_predictions: Anticipated the (n+l, then n) electron-filling rule eight years before Madelung's 1936 statement, purely from the regularity of the table; his block structure matches the quantum-mechanical aufbau pattern later established; ended his table at element 120, still the expected close of the period-8 s-block [INFERENCE: assessment of anticipation follows Stewart 2010]
citation: https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/006098575 (HathiTrust record of the 1928 Beauvais monograph, retrieved 2026-09-11); P. J. Stewart, "Charles Janet: unrecognized genius of the periodic system", Foundations of Chemistry 12 (2010) 5-15, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10698-008-9062-5 (retrieved 2026-09-11)

primary_source: Foundations: H. G. J. Moseley, "The High-Frequency Spectra of the Elements", Philosophical Magazine ser. 6 vol. 26 (1913), pp. 1024-1034, and Part II, vol. 27 (1914), pp. 703-713 (atomic number from X-ray spectra); current authority: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (18-column long form, periodically reissued; latest element approvals 2016)
organising_principle: Elements ordered by atomic number Z (nuclear charge, measured by Moseley's X-ray law); rows are quantum-mechanical shells with lengths 2,8,8,18,18,32,32 (2n^2 capacities); columns group identical valence-electron configurations
successful_predictions: Moseley's atomic-number sequence identified exactly the gaps Z=43,61,72,75, all later confirmed: hafnium (Coster and Hevesy, 1923), rhenium (Noddack, Tacke, Berg, 1925), technetium (Perrier and Segre, 1937), promethium (Marinsky, Glendenin, Coryell, 1945); framework predicted the completion of period 7 at Z=118, confirmed with oganesson (IUPAC verification 2015, named 2016)
citation: https://www.chemteam.info/Chem-History/Moseley-article.html (full text of Moseley 1913, retrieved 2026-09-11); https://iupac.org/what-we-do/periodic-table-of-elements/ (current IUPAC table, retrieved 2026-09-11)

primary_source: Robert W. Harrison, "The Spiral Periodic Table", spiralperiodictable.com (earliest Wayback capture 2011-04-08); formal write-up: Harrison, "The Spiral Periodic Table - Why Process Reveals What Classification Obscures", preprint, Feb 2026, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18078776; stated foundation: H. G. Deming, "General Chemistry: An Elementary Survey", New York: John Wiley & Sons, 1923 (18-column form, A/B subgroups, Group VIII linked to Group 0)
organising_principle: Continuous spiral by atomic number from lighter elements on the outer rim inward to heavier at the centre; 8 main-group (A) spokes with transition metals as an inner coil of 8 B-subgroups; Deming's Group VIIIB aligned radially with Group 0 (noble gases), justified via the 18-electron rule; period lengths explained as 2n^2
successful_predictions: None documented: the design is a re-visualisation of established chemistry (18-electron rule per Langmuir 1921/Sidgwick 1923 lineage; 2n^2 shell capacities from quantum mechanics); the site and preprint make no new-element or new-property predictions and the preprint states it does not claim to replace the conventional table

primary_source: Walter Russell, "The Universal One", New York: Brieger Press, c1926; chart "The Russell Periodic Chart of Atomic Weights, Electro-Magnetic Charge, Gravitation, Radiation, Sex, ..." at LoC image 0016; "Table of the Ten Octaves" pages (book p. 92 ff.)
organising_principle: Ten "octaves" of seven tones each (charge sequence 1+,2+,3+,4 double,3-,2-,1-) with mid-tones from the seventh octave onward; inert gases occupy the 0= equilibrium positions that end one octave and begin the next, drawn on the central "line of the inert gases"; hydrogen is tone 401+, the first positive element of the FOURTH octave, so three whole octaves of coined "unseen" elements (Alphanon, Betanon, Gammanon, Hydron, etc.) precede hydrogen
successful_predictions: No confirmed predictions; the coined pre-hydrogen elements and fourth-octave "helionon" (401-) remain undiscovered; atomic number Z=1 (hydrogen) is minimal by definition of nuclear charge, leaving no room for lighter elements [guardrail: deuterium/tritium "prediction" claims are excluded per project policy]
